subject: Request: 2yr frontloaded tiered prepay and ramp protection
messages:
From: Lina Gomez <lina@solarcraft.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: acme.finance@solarcraft.com
Date: Thu, 24 Sep 2026 15:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood eval — commercial ask

Marissa,

Thanks for the demo today — the team was impressed with the latency profiles and the autoscale story. Finance and I have run an initial model and we think a 2-year prepay with a frontloaded first year makes sense for SolarCraft, but we need clarity on the discount ladder and an explicit ramp protection.

High level ask: 2-year term, $1.2M committed value over 24 months, 65% of that paid in year 1 (frontload). We want guaranteed unit price protection if our usage jumps above 2.5x the forecast in any rolling quarter — ideally a capped step-up rather than full repricing.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can:
- Offer a tiered discount grid for a frontloaded prepay (targeting effective ~28% ARR discount)
- Provide a documented ramp protection clause (step-up caps at +35% pricing for overflow)
- Accept a quarterly true-up with a maximum effective true-up payment at contract midpoints

I'll attach the usage forecast and a short SOW draft for scope.

Thanks,
Lina Gomez
Head of Cloud Ops — SolarCraft

----
Attachment(s): usage_forecast_q3_q4.xlsx, SolarCraft_SOW_v1.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lina Gomez <lina@solarcraft.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood eval — commercial ask

Lina — really appreciate the clear asks and the forecast, that helps a lot.

Quick take: we can do a 2-year prepay with a frontloaded split (we typically see 60–70% frontload for these structures). We support a tiered discount grid; the specific % depends on committed ARR and expected QPS/sequence mix, but I can sketch a proposal:

- Baseline (0–100% of committed tokens/month): base prepay price (with your target ~28% blended discount as an achievable target)
- Overflow band 1 (100–250%): step price at +25% unit rate vs baseline (capped)
- Overflow band 2 (>250%): step price at +35% unit rate (this is our max step-up)

We can do quarterly true-ups and cap the quarterly step-up at the +35% as you asked. The SOW attachment looks fine; I'll circulate a rate table and a draft term sheet internally for approvals.

Proposed next step: I'll route a formal commercial term sheet for approval Monday; could you confirm whether SolarCraft needs amendments to Redwood's standard data residency or audit clauses?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

----
Attachment(s): none

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: SolarCraft commercial ask — margin/approval needed

Marissa — forwarding Lina's ask and your note. High level economics: $1.2M commit, 65% frontload means $780k upfront. Target blended discount ~28% gets near our threshold for a VP-level approval. Need Neha to confirm finance.

For legal/ops: Karthik, please confirm if the ramp protection language (step-up cap at +35% for overflow) is operationally enforceable — i.e., does the runtime support differentiated billing bands with a quarterly true-up and capped step-up? If we can do a clean billing band and a capped step-up we'll keep the commercial ask intact.

If Ops can't support banding precisely, we should propose a simplified alternative: a fixed per-token surcharge on overflow with a hard cap per quarter. That reduces billing complexity.

Requesting:
- Neha: margin check and whether we can approve at the director level or need VP sign-off
- Karthik: ops feasibility and estimate of any implementation lag or manual reconciliation effort

Thanks, Vivek
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: SolarCraft commercial ask — margin/approval needed

Vivek / team — ran preliminary margin models. Assuming the forecast distribution Lina provided and a blended discount of 28%, contribution margin before infra is approximately 38% on the committed volume and ~22% on expected overflow at current GPU mix.

Approveable under director delegation if:
- We keep overflow step-up capped at +35% (no deeper discounts)
- We add a quarterly ceiling on true-up exposure equal to 1.2x forecast for that quarter (limits short-term cash risk)
- Legal signs off on the amended billing bands and the reconciliation cadence

If SolarCraft insists on a higher blended discount (>30%), this needs VP approval. Also adding: require a minimum 30-day notice for any production-level configuration changes that materially affect token characteristics (so SRE has runway).

—Neha
Director, Finance — Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lina Gomez <lina@solarcraft.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Redwood eval — commercial ask

Lina — good news: finance has signed off under director delegation and Ops confirmed we can support tiered billing with a quarterly true-up. Key points for the term sheet (draft attached):

- Commitment: $1.2M over 24 months; payment schedule: 65% due within 30 days (Year 1 frontload), remaining 35% amortized across Year 2 in quarterly installments.
- Discount: target blended ~28% off list; final rate table attached in the term sheet.
- Overflow: pricing bands with step-up +25% (100–250%) and +35% (>250%); quarterly true-up with a quarterly cap (1.2x forecast for that quarter).
- Ops SLA/changes: 30-day notice for config changes affecting tokenization/throughput; Redwood to provide weekly telemetry for first 90 days post-prod.
- Attachments: SolarCraft_SOW_v1.pdf (scope), SolarCraft_term_sheet_draft_v1.pdf (rates & ramp language)

If that looks right, I'll push a DocuSign with the term sheet and proposed SOW next. We can also schedule a short call to walk legal through the billing bands.

Thanks — excited to get SolarCraft on board.

Best,
Marissa
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

----
Attachment(s): SolarCraft_term_sheet_draft_v1.pdf, SolarCraft_SOW_v1.pdf
